chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the injuries, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The injury of the woman is like the injury of the man until it reaches a third of the wergild (blood money). So when it reaches a third of the wergild, the injury of the man is doubled upon the injury of the woman; and the age of the man and the age of the woman are equal.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man kills a woman deliberately, and the family of the woman intend to kill the man, they should return half the wergild to the family of the man, and they kill him.'
He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who killed a man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She would be killed due to it, and her family would not be fined anything.'

key_terms.جِرَاحَة: Injury (specifically in the context of blood money compensation)
key_terms.يَغْرَمُ: To be fined / liable for payment

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in blood money and retaliation rules between men and women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between minor and major injuries, establishing that while compensation is equal up to one-third of the full blood money, the man's share doubles thereafter due to the principle of 'half-diyah' for major wounds. It further elucidates the mechanics of qisas (retaliation) in mixed-gender homicide, noting that the woman's family must pay half the man's blood money to his heirs to secure his execution, whereas a woman killing a man results in her execution without any financial compensation to her family. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view on the asymmetry in financial liability and the directness of retaliation based on gender in cases of intentional killing.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the injuries, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The injuries of the woman are like the injuries of the man until it reaches a third of the wergild. So when it reaches to be the same as a third of the wergild, the injuries of the man is additional by double upon the injuries of the woman; but a tooth of the man and a tooth of the woman are equal’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If a man kills a woman deliberately, so the family of the woman intend that they kill the man, they should return half the wergild to the family of the man, and they can kill him’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who kills a man. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would be killed due to it, and there her family would not be fined anything’.
